fullDescription:
Ko Lanta's east coast, which almost nobody sees, because the resorts and the sunsets are all on the west.

Lanta Old Town is a single street of wooden shophouses built out over the water on stilts, dating from when this was the island's main port and a stop on the trading route between Phuket and Penang. Some of the buildings are a century old and still lived in. It is a Chinese-Thai and Muslim fishing community rather than a preserved attraction, so expect drying fish, boat repairs and a few cafes rather than a heritage display.

The mangrove half of the trip goes into the channels at Tung Yee Peng by longtail boat, whose shallow draught gets into water a speedboat cannot enter. Mangrove forest reads as ordinary from outside and makes sense with a guide: the prop roots are a nursery where juvenile fish and crabs shelter before moving out to the reef, and the forest takes the force of storm surge off the island behind it. Mudskippers, crabs and kingfishers are the usual sightings, and the water sits almost still.

This is a good choice on a windy or wet day. Mangrove channels are sheltered, so the trip runs in conditions that cancel the open-sea island tours between May and October.

Oh-Hoo runs this and we book with them directly, so your place is held with the operator before the booking is final. The price covers hotel round-trip transfer, lunch with drinking water and fruit, a life jacket, a local English-speaking guide and basic accident insurance.

Five hours on Ko Lanta, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Lanta Old Town: stilt shophouses on the quiet east coast
A working fishing community, not a heritage display
Longtail into the Tung Yee Peng mangrove channels
Sheltered water, so it runs when island trips cancel
Lunch, guide, life jacket and transfers included

fullDescription:
The Krabi island circuit run backwards, so you are on the water for the part of the day everyone else misses.

Most boats leave Ao Nang in the morning, hit the same beaches at the same time as twenty other boats, and are back by mid-afternoon. This one departs later and works through the islands as the crowds thin out. By the time you reach the last stops the day-trip fleet has gone and the light has turned, which is the whole argument for booking the afternoon version.

The route covers seven islands off the Krabi coast with snorkelling where the water is clear and the reef is shallow enough to be worth it. Sunset is taken from the boat, and dinner follows. If conditions are right the trip finishes with bioluminescent plankton, which glows around your hands and feet when the water is disturbed. That part depends on the moon: dark nights near a new moon give the strongest display and a full moon washes it out entirely, so treat it as a bonus rather than the reason you booked.

A speedboat covers seven stops in seven hours comfortably. It is a long afternoon and evening rather than a relaxed one.

The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off in selected areas, round-trip speedboat transfer, a professional English-speaking guide, life jacket, snorkelling equipment, drinking water and seasonal fruit. We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

Seven hours, minimum one day's notice. Bring a towel and dry clothes.
highlights: Afternoon departure, so the islands are emptying out
Seven stops with snorkelling over shallow reef
Sunset taken from the water, dinner after
Plankton if the moon is dark, treated as a bonus
Speedboat, guide, snorkel gear and hotel pickup

fullDescription:
A long day out of Krabi into the oldest rainforest in the world, and onto a lake that did not exist fifty years ago.

Khao Sok National Park protects a forest estimated at around 160 million years old, which makes it considerably older than the Amazon. It survived the ice ages that reshaped most other tropical forests, and the result is a density of plant species and a landscape of limestone towers pushing straight up out of the canopy.

Cheow Lan Lake is the artificial part. The Rajjaprabha Dam flooded the valley in 1987, drowning the forest floor and leaving the karst peaks standing as islands. That is why the scenery looks the way it does: sheer limestone rising out of flat emerald water, with drowned tree trunks still visible near the shallows. Longtail boats work between the peaks, and the scale only registers once you are underneath them.

The drive from Krabi is roughly two and a half hours each way, which is most of the reason this is a ten-hour day. Wildlife sightings are a matter of luck: gibbons are heard more often than seen, hornbills are common along the shoreline, and macaques are a certainty near the boat piers.

The price covers hotel pickup from Krabi Town, Ao Nang, Klong Muang and Tub Kaek, an air-conditioned van, water, coffee and fruit, lunch at a restaurant, and a life jacket, raincoat and waterproof bag. We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

Ten hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Rainforest estimated at 160 million years old
Cheow Lan Lake, created by the Rajjaprabha Dam in 1987
Limestone peaks standing as islands in flat green water
Longtail boat between the karsts
Hotel pickup, van, lunch and wet-weather gear included

fullDescription:
An hour and a half in the canopy behind Ao Nang, on a course that can be dialled up or down depending on who is in your group.

The platforms are built into the trees on the slope above town, which puts you at the height where the forest actually happens: most of the movement and noise in tropical forest is in the canopy rather than at ground level. The lines run between platforms with limestone and the coastline visible through the gaps.

What you do depends on the option you book. The shorter family setup keeps the heights modest and adds game stations between the lines, so younger children get a course they can complete rather than a scaled-down version of an adult one. The longer options add more lines, more height and obstacle sections between platforms.

Guides run the course with you rather than sending you down alone, clipping and unclipping at each platform. No experience is needed and nothing requires upper-body strength; the harness does the work. The main thing to know is that it is a rainforest slope, so the ground is uneven and shoes matter more than they sound like they should.

Aonang Fiore Zipline Adventure runs this and we book with them directly, so your place is held with the operator before the booking is final. The price covers the zipline course, game stations according to the option selected, all safety equipment and expert guides. The operator emails the meeting point and time once your booking is confirmed.

Ninety minutes, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Canopy platforms on the slope behind Ao Nang
Family option with lower lines and game stations
Longer courses add height and obstacle sections
Guides clip and unclip at every platform
No experience or upper-body strength needed

fullDescription:
Phi Phi from Krabi rather than from Phuket, which shortens the crossing and changes the order you arrive in.

The Phi Phi group is two main islands. Phi Phi Don is the inhabited one, a narrow sand isthmus with a village between two bays, and Phi Phi Leh is uninhabited and is where Maya Bay sits. Maya Bay was closed entirely from 2018 to 2022 so the reef could recover, and it reopened under strict rules: boats moor at the back of the island and visitors walk in, swimming in the bay itself is restricted, and daily numbers are capped. Any operator promising you a swim in Maya Bay is describing something that no longer happens.

The rest of the day covers Pileh Lagoon, a channel of still green water enclosed by cliffs, Viking Cave with its rock paintings, and Monkey Beach, where the macaques are genuinely aggressive about food and worth keeping your distance from. Snorkelling stops depend on the sea and the guide picks them on the day.

Going from Krabi means a shorter run than from Phuket and a better chance of reaching the main stops before the Phuket boats do.

The price covers hotel transfer, the premium speedboat, buffet lunch, snorkelling equipment, drinking water, seasonal fruit, a professional guide, life jacket and travel insurance. National park fees are collected separately at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

Seven hours from Ao Nang, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Shorter crossing from Krabi than from Phuket
Maya Bay under post-2022 rules: walk in, capped numbers
Pileh Lagoon, Viking Cave and Monkey Beach
Snorkelling stops chosen on the day for conditions
Speedboat, buffet lunch, guide and insurance included

fullDescription:
Three and a half hours in the mangrove channels, finishing with seafood at a restaurant built over the water.

Krabi's mangrove belt runs along the river and out through the estuary, and the longtail boat is the right vehicle for it. Its shallow draught and long-shaft propeller let it work into channels barely wider than the hull, where the canopy closes overhead and the engine gets throttled down to almost nothing.

What you are looking at is a nursery. The tangled prop roots trap sediment and shelter juvenile fish, crabs and prawns until they are large enough to move out to the reef, which is why the fishing around Krabi depends on forest rather than open water. Mudskippers sit on the mud at low tide, kingfishers work the channel edges, and monitor lizards are common. Low tide exposes the root systems and is the more interesting half of the tide cycle to be there.

Lunch is fried rice with fruit and drinks at the Mangrove Seafood Restaurant, which sits on stilts at the water's edge.

This trip is sheltered from the open sea, so it runs during the green season from May to October when wind and swell cancel the island boats. If your island day gets called off, this is the substitute that still works.

The price covers round-trip hotel transfer, the longtail boat tour, fried rice with fruit and drinks, lunch at the restaurant, a local guide and insurance. We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

Three and a half hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Longtail into channels barely wider than the boat
The nursery that Krabi's fishing actually depends on
Mudskippers, kingfishers and monitor lizards
Runs in green season when island boats are cancelled
Seafood lunch at a stilt restaurant, transfers included

fullDescription:
The trip is named after a cave you can only reach by swimming through the dark, which is the part people remember.

Morakot Cave, the Emerald Cave, is on Ko Mook. The entrance is a low opening in the cliff and the only way in is to swim an eighty-metre tunnel, part of it in complete darkness, usually holding a rope with a guide leading. The tunnel opens into a hidden beach enclosed by vertical walls with sky directly overhead and the water lit green from the tunnel behind you. It is genuinely a swim, not a boat ride, and the entrance is tide-dependent: at high tide the gap can close entirely, which is why departure times shift with the tide rather than the clock.

Ko Chueak is the snorkelling stop, with soft coral and reef fish in shallow water close to the cliff. The other islands on the route are beach and swim stops.

The boat is a traditional longtail out of Ko Lanta Old Town Pier. Eight hours is a full day and there is limited shade on board, so a hat and a shirt you can swim in matter more than they would on a speedboat.

If you are not confident swimming in the dark, say so when you book. The guides take people through, but it is a real tunnel and not a walkway.

The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, the boat trip, guide, lunch, drinking water, fruit, life jacket, snorkelling masks and a first aid kit on board. We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

Eight hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Swim an 80-metre dark tunnel into the Emerald Cave
Hidden beach with vertical walls and open sky above
Entry is tide-dependent, so departure times move
Snorkelling over soft coral at Ko Chueak
Longtail from Lanta Old Town, lunch and gear included

fullDescription:
The classic Krabi day, done on a longtail rather than a speedboat, and timed around a sandbar that only exists for part of the day.

Thale Waek, the Separated Sea, is a strip of sand that emerges at low tide and joins Tup, Mor and Chicken islands into one walkable spit. At high tide it is simply gone. That is why this trip is scheduled by the tide table and not by a fixed departure time, and why a photograph of people standing in the middle of the sea is possible here at all.

Chicken Island is named for the rock formation at its tip, which reads as a chicken's head from the right angle and as nothing much from the wrong one. The snorkelling is on shallow coral just off the beach. Phra Nang has the cave shrine, where fishermen leave carved offerings to a spirit believed to protect them at sea, and it is one of the better beaches in Thailand independent of that. Tup and Poda are swimming and lying-down stops.

The longtail matters. It is slower than a speedboat, it is noisier, and it gets you into shallow water that speedboats have to anchor away from. Going with a local captain also means the route flexes with the sea rather than sticking to a schedule.

The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, the longtail with a local captain, an English-speaking guide, lunch, snorkelling equipment, drinking water, fruit, life jackets and insurance. National park fees are collected at the pier, so carry cash. We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

Seven hours, pickup in Ao Nang or Krabi Town, departing Nopparat Thara pier. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Walk the Thale Waek sandbar, which only appears at low tide
Departure timed to the tide, not to a fixed clock
Snorkel shallow coral off Chicken Island
The cave shrine at Phra Nang beach
Longtail with a local captain, lunch and gear included
